ac_findings.criterion: both tables live inside each tenant's Postgres schema with tenant_id retained
ac_findings.evidence: priv/repo/migrations/20260831000001_create_effect_completions.exs and 20260831000002_create_correlation_cursors.exs both have `if prefix() do` guard (tenant-scoped). Both are registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.@tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (lines 477+479 of tenant_provisioning.ex). Both tables include tenant_id column (non-null). Confirmed per-tenant placement matches decision 0003 Decision B.

ac_findings.criterion: inserting the same (correlation_id, sequence_no) twice results in ONE row and exactly ONE applied effect
ac_findings.evidence: Letflow.Ordering.insert_completion/2 uses `on_conflict: :nothing, conflict_target: [:correlation_id, :sequence_no]`. On conflict, re-reads the existing row via Repo.get_by and returns `{:ok, existing_row}`. The UNIQUE index on (correlation_id, sequence_no) is created in the migration. Test verified: 18/18 passed including idempotency tests.

ac_findings.criterion: completions apply strictly in sequence order; inserting seq 6 before seq 5 leaves 6 PENDING; after 5 is inserted and applied, 6 applies
ac_findings.evidence: consumer.ex M5 check: `if completion.sequence_no != cursor.applied_seq + 1 do Repo.rollback(:not_next) end`. Returns :not_next (not an error), row stays PENDING. Ordering confirmed by claiming lowest (correlation_id, sequence_no) via ORDER BY. 18/18 tests pass including the out-of-order scenario.

ac_findings.criterion: a completion whose sequence is not applied_seq + 1 rolls back silently: row stays PENDING, no error raised, no event appended
ac_findings.evidence: consumer.ex M5: `Repo.rollback(:not_next)` — rollback prevents event append (M6 not reached). try_apply/2 unwraps `{:error, :not_next}` to `:not_next` atom (no error tuple returned). Row status unchanged (still :pending) because transaction rolled back.

ac_findings.criterion: cursor advance is conditional; two concurrent applies of same sequence — exactly one success, one rolled-back re-claim
ac_findings.evidence: cursor.ex advance_conditional/3 uses `UPDATE ... WHERE applied_seq = ^expected_current`, returns :ok on count=1, :race on count=0. consumer.ex M8: `:race -> Repo.rollback(:cursor_race)`. try_apply/2 unwraps to :cursor_race. Transaction atomic — double-apply structurally impossible.

ac_findings.criterion: a correlation with no cursor row applies its first completion successfully, initialising cursor rather than failing
ac_findings.evidence: consumer.ex M3: inserts Cursor with applied_seq=0 using `on_conflict: :nothing`. Cursor.upsert_init/2 in cursor.ex also implements the same via `on_conflict: :nothing, conflict_target: :correlation_id`. M4 then reads the cursor (applied_seq=0), M5 allows seq_no=1 through. 18/18 tests pass including first-apply scenario.

ac_findings.criterion: two different correlations both apply — neither serialised behind the other
ac_findings.evidence: consumer.ex M2 advisory lock key: `:erlang.phash2(correlation_id, 2_147_483_647)` — different correlation_ids hash to different keys (collision probability safe at S6 scale per moduledoc). pg_try_advisory_xact_lock is transaction-scoped. 18/18 tests pass including parallel-correlation test.

ac_findings.criterion: sweeper moves EVERY PENDING row of affected correlation to DEAD as one unit; creates exactly one DLQ entry; a correlation at exactly applied_seq+1 is NOT swept
ac_findings.evidence: sweeper.ex find_eligible_correlations SQL HAVING clause: `MIN(ec.sequence_no) > COALESCE(cc.applied_seq, 0) + 1` (strict greater-than, not >=). sweep_correlation/2 uses single transaction: UPDATE all PENDING to DEAD + Dlq.enqueue in one Repo.transaction. Rolls back entirely if DLQ fails. 18/18 tests pass including both the sweep and non-sweep cases.

ac_findings.criterion: sweeper gap_timeout is configurable; correlation younger than timeout not swept even when predecessor absent
ac_findings.evidence: sweeper.ex gap_timeout_seconds/0: `Application.get_env(:letflow, :ordering, []) |> Keyword.get(:gap_timeout_seconds, 300)`. HAVING clause: `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - MIN(ec.created_at))) > $1` — strict greater-than. 18/18 tests pass including configurable-timeout test.

ac_findings.criterion: consumer does not hold a DB connection across poll interval; asserted by test running cycle against smaller pool without exhausting it
ac_findings.evidence: consumer.ex: claim/1 opens and closes its own Repo.transaction. try_apply/2 opens and closes its own Repo.transaction. Both return before run_cycle/2 returns. ordering.ex run_cycle/2 doc: 'Acquires and releases a database connection within this single call — never held across the poll sleep'. 18/18 tests pass including pool-discipline test.

ac_findings.criterion: subsystem is wired on REQ-186's scheduler; running cycle applies a completion end-to-end without manual invocation; application.ex not changed
ac_findings.evidence: poller.ex lines 118-120: `maybe_run_ordering_cycle(schemas)`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper(schemas)`, `maybe_run_ordering_metrics(schemas)` called in handle_info(:tick, state). All three private functions in poller.ex call Letflow.Ordering.run_cycle/2, sweep_gaps/2, emit_lag_metrics/2 respectively. git diff --stat ba4915fa...HEAD shows NO changes to lib/letflow/application.ex. 18/18 tests pass including end-to-end wired test.

ac_findings.criterion: effect-applied event type is registered in per-tenant event_type_registry so REQ-025 ES-05 check accepts it
ac_findings.evidence: tenant_provisioning.ex @platform_event_type_seed_attrs line 920: `name: "effect_applied"` and line 936: `name: "ordering_lag_threshold_exceeded"` — both present. Seeded into event_type_registry during provisioning. Confirmed by full test run: test log shows INSERT INTO event_type_registry for both event types.

ac_findings.criterion: per-correlation lag = max(sequence_no) - applied_seq; correlation with seq 1..5 and applied_seq 2 reports lag 3; fully-applied reports 0
ac_findings.evidence: metrics.ex compute_all_lags/1 SQL: `MAX(ec.sequence_no) - COALESCE(cc.applied_seq, 0) AS lag`. WHERE ec.status = 'PENDING' means only correlations with PENDING rows appear (fully-applied correlations with no pending rows return lag=0 via empty result set → write_to_registry computes max_lag=0 from empty list). 18/18 tests pass including both lag=3 and lag=0 cases.

ac_findings.criterion: age of oldest PENDING row reported per correlation; correlation with no PENDING rows reports nil (not zero)
ac_findings.evidence: metrics.ex compute_all_lags/1: WHERE ec.status = 'PENDING' — correlations with no PENDING rows do not appear in results. compute_platform_maximums/1: `case [] -> nil` for ages. write_to_registry writes nil for max_age when lags list is empty. For non-empty correlations, oldest_pending_age_seconds is computed from MIN(received_at). 18/18 tests pass.

ac_findings.criterion: crossing configured lag threshold emits lag event with correlation_id, lag, and oldest_pending_age_seconds in payload
ac_findings.evidence: metrics.ex emit_threshold_exceeded_event/4: Jason.encode! with keys `correlation_id`, `lag`, `oldest_pending_age_seconds`. Called when `lag > threshold` in write_to_registry. EventStore.append_platform_event used. All 3 required fields present in payload. 18/18 tests pass including threshold-exceeded test.

ac_findings.criterion: moduledoc states ORD-04 dynamic consumer-count reduction is deliberately deferred; R-Co also left it unimplemented; deferred half depends on REQ-194
ac_findings.evidence: ordering.ex moduledoc lines 8-16: 'ORD-04's dynamic consumer-count reduction under contention is deliberately deferred and NOT implemented here. R-Co itself left this half unimplemented in production (its ordering subsystem was unwired — Letflow corrects that gap, but does not add the deferred reduction). The deferred half depends on REQ-194's metrics registry being established (which it now is), but the reduction algorithm itself (backoff heuristics, consumer-count configuration source) requires a separate design.' All three elements present.

ac_findings.criterion: no route or controller file added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to requirement's commits
ac_findings.evidence: git diff --stat ba4915fa...HEAD output: only 5 files changed — handoffs/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, step-02d-reviewer.json, step-03b-test-design-validator.json; test/letflow/ordering_test.exs; test/specs/REQ-199.md. Zero routers/ or controllers/ files appear.

Result: 2933/2935 passed. Failed: 2 tests' — both pre-existing Windows grep :enoent (Lua.SandboxTest, Wasm.HostApiTest), not regressions.

notes: Cursor.upsert_init/2 in cursor.ex is a standalone public function (NB-1 from REVIEWER step-02d). It is also duplicated inline in consumer.ex M3. Both paths use on_conflict: :nothing, so correctness is unaffected. Not a blocker.
metrics.ex idempotency key uses System.os_time(:millisecond) (NB-4 from REVIEWER). This means rapid successive calls could emit duplicate events. Not a blocker at S6 scale.
Both failures in the full suite are pre-existing Windows-only failures (grep :enoent) introduced before REQ-199 — confirmed by re-running mix test --failed and verifying error messages.
